events.summary:
H1 is adequately proven and is now the only hypothesis standing. Its causal chain is verified end-to-end at the auth-service-local level and temporally coherent: F6 (request_rate ~380-405 -> ~1450-1538 req/s, ~3.9x, in the 06:50Z bucket) coincides to the bucket with F1 (p99 88-92ms -> 3.8s) and F5 (CPU ~37-40% -> pinned 96-98%, memory flat 51-53%); F4 verifies the mechanism (worker pool 64/64 active, accept-queue backlog up to 98763, autoscaler desiring 14 replicas capped at maxReplicas=8); F3/F2 verify the effect (app-level admission control 'accept queue full' 503s, 14%, first at 06:55:42Z, one bucket after the latency jump). F39 corroborates login-path excess (rate_limited ~450x). The gateway is confirmed a pass-through, not an origin (F24-F29, F36-F38): its request step and the gateway's ~3.9-4.1x multiplier match auth-service's ~3.8x, it stays flat on CPU/memory with 0 restarts and 0 ERROR logs, and its error_rate/p99 (06:54Z) lag its own request step (06:50Z) and mirror auth-service. H3 was rejected by direct measurement at redis-cache (F18-F23: hit_ratio flat and locally HIGH at onset, evictions flat, clients flat, CPU ~21-23% while auth CPU pinned ~96%, zero WARN+ logs). H2 has no trigger: deployment sweeps covering 01:00-09:00Z (F30, F13, F7, F32) found zero auth-service releases and zero changes to user-db/redis-cache/login path; the only config change anywhere is a 03:40Z logging-verbosity edit ~3h10m pre-onset (F8/F31); the 04:00-09:00Z config sweep is empty (F14). HIST-101's bcrypt signature matches but its deployment trigger is demonstrably absent (F11/F13/F32). H4 is weak-by-construction (no telemetry) and contradicted by the CPU-pinned, non-IO-wait, 'accept queue full' signature (F3/F5).

Residual uncertainty is confined to a SECONDARY detail of an established origin, not to competing origins: the per-route login multiplier cannot be measured (F34/F40/F44 - no route dimension exists on any service), so the route axis that could in principle distinguish 'pure external demand' from a 'load-amplified per-request-cost' variant is unresolvable. But both variants name the SAME service and the SAME origin (auth-service capacity outgrown by offered load through the gateway), and F38 shows the auth-service and gateway multipliers match within noise, which is what H1 predicts and what a small-login-surge-plus-per-request-cost story does not. The one genuinely unresolved number (the ~3.2x absolute gateway-vs-auth delta, F38) is a composition artifact of a per-service proxy conflating route with upstream, and no available tool can resolve it - so it is uncertainty about a detail, expressed as a confidence cap and an assumption, not a reason for inconclusive. Critically, no alternative origin with a DIFFERENT fix survives: the shared-infrastructure origin (H3) is eliminated by measurement, the deployment origin (H2) has no trigger in a now-continuous change record, the gateway origin (H5) is a demonstrated unsaturated pass-through, and H4 has no telemetry support and a contradicting signature. Therefore the choice set is not two differently-named origins - it is one origin with an unmeasurable sub-detail. Round 3 closed the last deployment-coverage hole (T8/F30: 01:00-05:30Z = count 0), so no further query would change the ranking. Fix direction is well defined regardless of sub-detail: relieve auth-service capacity/provisioning (and rate-limit or absorb the external login demand) - not a rollback of an auth-service release, which H2 would have required.

Caveats carried forward as assumptions, not blockers: (a) the ~3.9x request_rate step is genuine offered load, not a metric artifact - supported by its coincidence with independent CPU, queue-depth and rate-limit counters but not independently metered per route; (b) whether non-login auth routes also degraded is unresolvable (aggregate metrics only, route-agnostic 64/64 pool), but worker-pool saturation is a process-wide shared resource, so all-route exhaustion is the better-supported reading; (c) the identity of the demand generator (client event vs retry storm) remains unidentified - this does not change the origin or the fix direction.
